name: Shelly Cove Trail / Shelly Beach Trail
description:
Saturday 4 July 2026 - 6:30 am
Location: Cape Pallarenda Conservation Park / Townsville Town Common
Leader: Amanda
RSVP: ajdrill@gmail.com
Places: Limited to 15
Distance: Approx. 8 km
Grade: S23
S = Duration: Short - under 4 hours
2 = Terrain: Mostly track, or easy open country with minor uneven ground
3 = Fitness: Moderate - suitable for active walkers
Easy to moderate, mostly formed tracks, beach sections, soft sand, minor uneven ground, and very little elevation gain.
https://townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/club-walk-grading-system/
Walk type: Loop, with some beach walking

Join Amanda this Saturday morning for a relaxed coastal walk through the Cape Pallarenda and Townsville Town Common trail network, taking in the Shelly Cove / Shelly Beach area.

This walk follows a mix of formed tracks, coastal woodland, open country, and beach sections, with views across Cleveland Bay and towards Magnetic Island. Along the way, the group may pass WWII-era features, coastal scrub, mangroves, seasonal wetlands, and quieter sections of the shoreline.

The route is relatively flat, with only minor elevation gain, but walkers should still be prepared for soft sand, exposed sections, uneven surfaces, and warm conditions. Some of the tracks are shared with mountain bike riders, so please stay alert and give way where needed.

Please bring water, sun protection, insect repellent, suitable footwear, and snacks. As this walk includes coastal areas, please also be croc-wise and avoid entering the water.

RSVP to Amanda at ajdrill@gmail.com for meeting details.

The events are free for members and non-members. However, after completing three club walks, you must apply to become a member.

Clicking "Going" on Facebook does not register you for the event. Also, note that the location listed on the Facebook Event is not necessarily where we are meeting. The meeting location and final details will be emailed to you by the walk leader once you have RSVP'd.

Please read the Townsville Bushwalking Club’s Walker Guidelines and What to Bring information on the club website before attending.

name: Hidden Gorges - Private Property
description:
When: Saturday 4 July to Monday 6 July 2026
Leaders: Keith and Wilfred
Grade: L67RC
L = Duration: Long - 6 to 8 hours
6 = Terrain: Difficult off-track terrain, steep creek beds, frequent rock hopping, hands-on scrambling
7 = Fitness: Strenuous - fit walkers only
R = Modifier: Remote - difficult retreat, long rescue time, limited exit options
C = Modifier: Climb - significant elevation gain or steep sustained ascent/descent
Best estimate only until the final route is known. Hard multi-day car-camp trip with full-day gorge exploration, steep climbs, rugged creek terrain, remoteness, and likely route-finding. 
https://townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/club-walk-grading-system/
So Medium Hard. Rough terrain, bushbashing, rock hopping, exposed ledges, some steep hills.
Duration: Three-day car-camp and walking trip
RSVP: kadyson@hotmail.com

Numbers are limited to 12 pax and 4 cars (4WDs).

Members wishing to participate are to register with Keith Dyson directly - kadyson@hotmail.com

Full details will be provided to registered participants.

Members have priority, but numbers are limited to 12 participants only (also subject to suitable vehicles and car sharing availability).

Registered participants are requested to attend the club AGM on 29th June for final briefing and arrangements. It is important to have participants at the meeting so that we can finalise plan for timings, cars, re-brief requirements and check understanding of what is involved, and property owner access requirements.

We have permission from the private property owner.

Who is this suitable for ? Suitable for experienced, well equipped, remote and rough terrain capable bushwalkers. Must be self-sufficient for three days remote bush camping– no support available. No facilities or infrastructure  (water is available from natural creek sources).

What’s the Plan? A three day adventure. Drive in Saturday morning, walk to camp site, set-up camp. Camp site is in the creek bed (sandy) approx 500 metres walk-in from car park.

Camping Saturday and Sunday night in the creek. Day walks on Saturday, Sunday and Monday from base camp site in the gorge system (bushwalking with day packs only). Drive out Monday at time TBC.

What do we see ? A spectacular gorge system.

Trip coord is Keith. Any questions please direct to Keith. Walk Leaders – Keith and Wilfred.

Access is subject to terms and conditions of the property owner. Full details of these will be provided to registered participants. Some key points are included at bottom of this notice.

What do we need ? 4WD high clearance vehicles with recovery points. Car share is encouraged and required to fit 12 people.

Costs
The events are free for members and non-members. However, after completing three club walks, you must apply to become a member.

Car sharing costs – arrangement between the driver and passenger(s). Suggest car share costs and conditions are known to your passenger(s) before the trip start so no surprises at end of journey.

Property Access Conditions (to be re-confirmed)

Final approval is subject to risk assessment process of the club activity by the property manager.

Visiting the property is subject to terms and conditions of the property owner. Full copy of conditions will be provided to participants.

Of particular note:
All vehicles entering the property must be washed down to remove weed seed before traveling around the sanctuary.

Only high clearance 4WD vehicles fitted with recovery points are allowed beyond the homestead

All visitors must undergo a site induction and sign the Visitor Log (form C) upon arrival.

You are the person primarily responsible for your own safety.

Photography and filming
• You may take photos or film for private or personal use only.
• Drones are prohibited.
• Copies of photos or film taken may be requested, and you must consent to publication if requested.
• If you would like to make photos or footage that you take publicly available, provide them to a third party to publish, or use them for commercial purposes, you must obtain written consent prior to your visit. This includes Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, X, Flickr, personal websites, etc.

name: North Creek
description:
When: Sunday 12 July 2026
Location: North Creek, Bowling Green Bay National Park
Leader: Amanda
RSVP: ajdrill@gmail.com
Grade: M55
M = Duration: Medium - 4 to 6 hours
5 = Terrain: Sustained rough terrain, creek walking, boulder hopping, moderate scrub, and some scrambling
5 = Fitness: Moderate to hard - sustained effort over rough terrain, including a steep climb
Approximately 11.5 km return, following North Creek through granite creek country, waterfalls, boulder fields, steep ridges, and off-track terrain.
https://townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/club-walk-grading-system/
AWTGS = 5 - off-track creek walking, rock hopping, scrambling, bush bashing, steep slopes, and rough terrain
Distance: Approximately 11.5 km return
Duration: Allow approximately 5-6 hours

Join Amanda for an adventurous off-track walk into North Creek, also known as Sandy Creek, in Bowling Green Bay National Park. Once used by the Townsville Bushwalking Club as an introductory off-track walk, this route offers granite creek scenery, waterfalls, rock pools, mountain views, and a rewarding swimming hole beneath the upper falls.

The walk begins on established tracks before leaving the formed trail and following North Creek upstream. The route involves sustained rock-hopping, boulder scrambling, creek-walking, and navigating around waterfalls and rocky obstacles. Some sections may require short climbs over rock slabs or detours through vegetation. The exact route is undecided, but we normally walk up the ridgeline for most of it to avoid the large boulders near the bottom. 

Beyond the lower waterfalls and fig tree pool, the terrain becomes steeper and more rugged. The group will generally leave the creek and climb onto the western ridgeline, sometimes known as Horse Ridge, to avoid the largest boulders and drop-offs. This section includes a steep, scrambly climb and a faint, unformed route through the bush.

The goal will be the upper North Creek falls, approximately 530 m above sea level. Depending on conditions, time, and the group's progress, there may be an opportunity to descend to the pool beneath the falls for lunch and a refreshing swim.

Although North Creek has traditionally been considered a good introduction to off-track walking, participants must be aware that it's not an easy formed-track hike and that they must be comfortable moving over uneven, slippery rocks, scrambling around boulders, walking through vegetation, and climbing steep, unformed terrain. Good balance, confidence on rough ground, and a reasonable level of fitness are required.

The final route and turnaround point may be adjusted by the walk leader depending on weather, creek conditions, group progress, and time.

Bring:

* At least 2 L of water, with 3 L recommended
* Lunch, morning tea, and snacks
* Sturdy footwear with good grip
* Sun protection
* Insect repellent
* Long sleeves and/or long pants for vegetation
* Swimmers and a small towel
* First aid kit with compression bandages
* Personal locator beacon, if you have one
* A waterproof bag for items that need to remain dry

name: Mt Stuart Road fitness walk
description:
Mt Stuart Road fitness walk - Tuesday mornings
Date: Tuesday 14th July 2026
When: Tuesdays, 4:45 am
Location: Mt Stuart Road, Townsville
Leaders: Wilfred
RSVP: wilfred.suzanne@bigpond.com.au
Grade: S15C
S = Duration: Short - under 4 hours
1 = Terrain: Formed track, fire trail, or very easy open terrain
5 = Fitness: Solid - good fitness needed for a full day out
C = Modifier: Climb - significant elevation gain or steep sustained ascent/descent
Short on time, but a steady 15 km bitumen climb to the summit and back. Terrain is easy; fitness demand is the main factor - but walk at your own pace.
https://townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/club-walk-grading-system/
The meeting location will be sent to those who RSVP.

Wilfred's regular Tuesday Mt Stuart road walk is open to club members who want a solid pre-dawn fitness hit. We will meet at 4:45 am and walk the bitumen road all the way to the 584 m summit and back, covering approximately 15 km return. This is a self-paced, steady uphill grind followed by a controlled descent - ideal for building endurance and leg strength. We walk up for 1.5 hours, which usually means we rest at the top and then go back down again ~1.5 hours.

As usual, we will bring a small bag and pick up rubbish along the way, giving the mountain a bit of care while we train. Bring water and a head torch, and be prepared for exposed conditions once the sun rises. No frills, just consistent effort, good company and sunrise views over Gurrumbilbarra.

name: Godwin's Peak, Paluma
description:
When: Sunday 19 July 2026
Location: Paluma Range National Park / Clement State Forest
Leader: Cherry Judge
RSVP: info@veteducation.com.au
Places: Limited to 15
Grade: X67NRC
X = Duration: Extra long - more than 8 hours
6 = Terrain: Difficult off-track terrain, steep creek beds, frequent rock hopping, hands-on scrambling
7 = Fitness: Very hard - strong fitness and stamina required
N = Modifier: Navigation critical - off-track route-finding or poor visibility of route
R = Modifier: Remote - difficult retreat, long rescue time, limited exit options
C = Modifier: Climb - significant elevation gain or steep sustained ascent/descent
Long, strenuous summit walk with steep climbing, rough marked route, creek crossings, rock hopping, remote terrain, and navigation awareness required.
https://townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/club-walk-grading-system/
AWTGS=5 - difficult and strenuous, preferably for experienced bushwalkers
Distance: Approximately 16 km return
Duration: Approximately 7-10 hours

Cherry will be leading a challenging day walk to Godwin's Peak, one of the most rewarding summits in the Paluma Range National Park area. Sitting at 783 metres elevation, Godwin's Peak offers spectacular 360-degree views across Mount Halifax, Townsville, the coastline, Mount Stuart, Castle Hill, Magnetic Island, and the surrounding ranges on a clear day.

The route begins along forestry vehicle tracks through Clement State Forest before entering rougher bushwalking terrain, with creek crossings, rock hopping, waterfalls, and a long, steep climb toward the summit. Highlights along the way include Twin Falls, Pick Falls, changing vegetation as the route gains elevation, and the open grassy summit with its impressive panoramic views.

This walk is rated Grade 5 and should be considered difficult and strenuous. The track is rough, uneven, steep, and sometimes more of a marked route than a well-formed trail. The climb is slow-going, especially near the upper ridgeline, and walkers should be comfortable with long distances, remote terrain, loose surfaces, creek crossings, and a full day in the bush. Moderate to high fitness and previous bushwalking experience are strongly recommended.

Bring:
- At least 3 L of water, plus a way to treat/filter creek water if needed
- Lunch and plenty of snacks
- Sturdy footwear with good grip
- Hat and sun protection
- Raincoat and warm layer, as the summit can be cool or wet
- First aid kit and compression bandage
- Head torch, in case the walk takes longer than expected
- Insect repellent
- Swimmers, if you would like a creek swim
- Dry bag for items you do not want to get wet
- Change of clothes for the trip home

Meeting details will be provided once you RSVP directly to Cherry at info@veteducation.com.au

name: Paradise Beach clean-up overnighter with Ocean Crusaders
description:
Date: Saturday 25 to Sunday 26 July 2026
Location: Paradise Beach
Leader: Brent
Places: Limited to 15
RSVP: Brent brentgc1306@gmail.com 
Places: Limited to 15
Grade: L45
L = Duration: Long - 6 to 8 hours
4 = Terrain: Off-track sections, loose ground, minor scrub, rock hopping, creek crossings
5 = Fitness: Solid - good fitness needed for a full day out
Remote coastal walk plus clean-up work, carrying overnight gear. Terrain is not highly technical, but remoteness, scrubby/overgrown sections, and pack weight lift the grade.
https://townsvillebushwalkingclub.com/club-walk-grading-system/
ATWGS=4 

Join the Townsville Bushwalking Club for a special overnight walk to Paradise Beach, combining a remote coastal adventure with a practical beach clean-up in support of Ocean Crusaders.

Ocean Crusaders will be coming through Townsville in June and July as part of their clean-up efforts, and Brent has been in touch with Kylie to help organise the removal of rubbish from Paradise Beach. They will drop off rubbish bags in advance, and our group will hike in on Saturday morning, help fill the bags during the day, camp overnight, and have the collected rubbish ready for pick-up at 7:00 am on Sunday morning before hiking back out.

Because the rubbish collection is early on Sunday, we will most likely need to camp close to the beach rather than up on the ridgeline. The final camping location and logistics will be confirmed with participants closer to the date.

Participants should be prepared for a remote overnight walk carrying all personal camping gear, food, water, and clean-up items. Please also bring work or gardening gloves, sturdy footwear, sun protection, and clothing suitable for beach work. Rubbish bags will be provided, but participants should take care around sharp, rusty, or hazardous objects and follow the leader’s instructions during the clean-up.

A day walk option may also be added if another leader is available to guide a group in and out on Saturday. Please let the leader know when you RSVP whether you are interested in the overnighter or a possible day-walk option.

This is a great opportunity to enjoy one of our special coastal places while giving something back to the environment and supporting the work of Ocean Crusaders.

The events are free for members and non-members. However, after completing three club walks, you must apply to become a member.
